statement: A disjoint set union (DSU, also called union–find) keeps elements in separate groups and supports two operations: find(x), which returns the representative of x's group, and union(u, v), which merges the groups of u and v.

Union by size hangs the root of the smaller group under the root of the larger one, so trees stay shallow, and path compression points each element a find passes straight at its representative. Together they make each operation almost constant time.

You are given dsu: its vertex count n is the number of elements, numbered 0 to n − 1, and its edges are union(u, v) operations to apply in order. Apply every union and return the final groups, each listed in increasing order.

examples.explanation: The first two unions build {1, 2} and {3, 4}. union(2, 1) finds both already in one group and changes nothing. Elements 0 and 5 are never mentioned, so each stays alone.
union(2, 4) joins the groups built by the first two unions into {1, 2, 3, 4}. union(5, 6) makes a separate pair, and 0 and 7 are untouched.
